images.title: A square has four fold lines
images.purpose: Show the four lines of symmetry of a square, each one a fold where the halves match.
images.composition: Four equal squares in one row with wide gaps, each with a single dashed line.
images.exact_structure: One row of exactly 4 equal squares, filled teal #0072B2. Each square has one dashed line in reddish purple #CC79A7 through its centre: square 1 upright, square 2 across, square 3 diagonal from top left to bottom right, square 4 diagonal from top right to bottom left. Numbers 1 to 4 below the squares, and one line of text centred below the row. Exactly 4 squares and 4 dashed lines.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a square with more than one dashed line, or fewer than 4 squares
images.takeaway: A square has four lines of symmetry.
images.description: Four equal teal squares in a row, each with one dashed fold line: upright, across and the two diagonals, numbered 1 to 4.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say how the halves match for each of the four fold lines, then count them.

image_decisions.why: The idea is a picture idea; one clean image carries it.
